Every major city in the world has its share of death. New Orleans just made an art form of it. In Murder Atlas: New Orleans Edition, you'll follow a trail of scandal, mystery, and blood through the city's shadowy past, where jazz music can literally save your life.

Track clues, interrogate suspects, and outrun the shadows in a city of jazz, ghosts, and unsolved horrors, where the legend of the Axeman still hangs in the air.

nodes.body: Despite the painful memories that seem to surface whenever Minnesota and New Orleans meet, one thing is undeniable: New Orleans is a great away game destination. Created by a New Orleans native, this "Takeover Game" just might be the best part of your trip, especially if your team loses.

nodes.body:
Buccaneers fans… it’s time to invade the Big Easy!
Grab your crew and join the ultimate scavenger hunt experience as Tampa Bay fans take over New Orleans! Race through the French Quarter, chase clues across iconic spots like Bourbon Street, Jackson Square, and beyond, snapping photos, completing wild challenges, and earning points for your squad.
Hunt for hidden Tampa Bay treasures, crush pirate-themed tasks, and prove once and for all that Bucs fans run this town (at least for one epic day). Bragging rights, prizes, and legendary memories are waiting!
Whether you’re in town for the game or just here to represent, this is the most fun you’ll have in New Orleans without getting thrown in jail.

name: Oswald's Diary

nodes.body:
What’s more peculiar than a ghost tour?

On August 9th, 1963, a well traveled 23-year-old man was arrested in New Orleans for disturbing the peace.

3 months later he was arrested in Dallas, and immediately became the presumptive assassin of President John F. Kennedy.

2 days later he too was fatally shot.

That young man was Lee Oswald.

Those are facts.

From here on out, anything you discover may be fact, or it may be fiction.

That's for you to decipher.

You've found Oswald's Diary.

Your mission is to take it to the city where he was born and get it into the right hands before it's too late.
